Addtional information for Doctoral Program
Taking a same subject that you took already in Master program as a Doctoral program course is not accepted as credits toward completion of Doctoral program.
* Please be careful not to take same courses more than once. Try searching for alternative courses in course registration programs
* In case you earn 6 credits of undergraduate courses in master program, you may not earn credits of undergraduate courses for completion of doctoral program.
2. Period of thesis submission
Master's dissertation: within 4 years after completion of Master course.
Doctoral dissertation: within 6 years after completion of Doctoral course.
3. Required documents for conferment of Doctoral degree
Student who plans to present a doctoral dissertation must submit the form (refer to announcement of the department) with 1 copy of summary and a confirmation letter from supervising professor, in accordance with the ‘Rule on Doctoral Degree Conferment (publishing in international journals), Department of Biological Sciences’.
(Doctoral Program) Applied to the students entering in 2004 and beyond.
(Combined Doctoral and Master Program) Applied to students entering in 2002 and beyond.

Curriculum for Graduate (students entering in year 2010 to 2018)
• Departmental Course Requirements
Students in Doctoral Program should take more than 3 courses and those in Master Program 2 courses listed in the ‘Core Courses,’ not including the course of Reading and Research (3344.803) for Molecular and Cellular Biology (MCB), Integrative Organismic Biology (IOB), and Systematics and Ecology (SE). For doctoral student, the Core Courses that he/she took in Master Program can be accredited at the time of evaluating the eligibility test for a doctoral dissertation.
Considering the Core Courses are reflected in the eligibility test for a doctoral dissertation, they (Core Courses) are graded as relative evaluations
[Transitional provision] The above 1-2 regulations are to be applied from the year 2010 entering students, and students enrolled prior to the 2009 academic year can choose from the existing regulations or current regulations.
Students entering in year 2015 and beyond are required to take the course of ‘Research Ethics (990.501A.001) before completion of degree courses. Research Ethics can be optionally taken by students entering before year 2015.
Detailed rules are fixed by private rules.
